newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro worries weigh on German shares at opening.
newsitem.headline: Euro worries weigh on German shares at opening.

text.p: Talk of a possible delay to the launch of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) pressured the jittery German share market early Friday, sparking fears for the outlook for exporters' earnings.
The 30-share DAX index was down 21.06 points at 3,255.66 points at 1008 GMT, extending mild early losses triggered by overnight decline on Wall Street and in Japan.
Dealers were unable to pinpoint the source of the rumours on EMU, but the market was awash with talk that Germany would today issue a statement on a delay.
"This is a very nervous market here and rumours like this are guaranteed to have people running scared. We need to have this clarified," said one futures dealer.
The March DTB DAX futures contract was down 19 points at 3,261 points in early bourse trade.

The slide slowed as the Bundesbank and the German Finance Ministry denied that they planned to issue a statement on EMU and dealers said the strong Bunds and firm dollar should offset any serious losses on the market.
Volumes were in any case low as the end of the month approached and many dealers closed their positions.
The declines were spread across the board, with most blue chip shares under pressure.

Volkswagen however was up 12 marks at 821 marks after the carmaker said on Thursday that sales in January rose 18 percent and it expected to maintain its world market share in 1997 despite difficult industry conditions.
Porsche also rose 10 marks to 1,935 after reporting its 1996/97 profits surged to 38.4 million marks from 10.3 million marks on the back of a 25.6 percent increase in sales to 1.78 billion marks.
